item.title: Eby says B.C. could fight lumber tariffs in U.S. courts
item.description: VICTORIA — British Columbia Premier David Eby says a ruling by the United States Supreme Court that strikes down far-reaching global tariffs opens the door to challenge other tariffs that currently hurt his province’s softwood lumber industry. item.title: OpenAI contacted RCMP about Tumbler Ridge shooter’s ChatGPT account after attack
item.description: ChatGPT employees considered alerting authorities about the account connected to the Tumbler Ridge shooter.

item.title: Dawson Creek ends drought ‘state of local emergency’ after water stores deemed enough for spring
item.description: Dawson Creek has ended its ‘state of local emergency’ (SOLE) because it believes its water stores from the Kiskatinaw River will last through spring 2026.

item.title: GoFundMe for other children of slain Tumbler Ridge mother collects more than $25,000
item.description: Amy Johann of Grande Prairie organized a GoFundMe for the children of Jennifer Strang, the mother who was killed by the Tumbler Ridge shooter on February 10th.

item.title: Officers search for man, 45, missing from Fort St. John
item.description: The Fort St. John RCMP are looking for missing Lyle Bremner.

item.title: Heli-skier dies in avalanche near Revelstoke, B.C.
item.description: REVELSTOKE — A heli-skier has died after being caught in an avalanche in southeastern British Columbia. RCMP say they were told on Thursday about a fatality after an avalanche in a heli-skiing area near Revelstoke, about 640 kilometres east of Vancouver. item.title: Cultural Gathering of Nations returns for 2026
item.description: The Cultural Gathering of Nations' event coordinator Daniel Desjarlais said more Treaty 8 B.C. Nations will participate in the event's logistics in 2026.
